metadata.title: Post-fix semantic re-check — 16 remaining REVIEW candidates
metadata.candidate_revision: Working tree after the Stage-5 fix pass, engine commit e8503cdfb32a83817a2fbc84ad4245057acf75a2 (HEAD at review time).
metadata.reviewer: Same base model as the drafter and as Model B (author-side semantic re-check).
metadata.independence: NONE. This is not an independent Model-B run and it is not cross-family validation. The reviewer had access to drafting context, which a true independent reviewer would not.
metadata.prior_review_note: batch-1..4 are the original Model-B verdicts on the checkpoint revision. batch-5 re-read 25 candidates, but several of its REVIEW reasons describe pre-fix text that the shipped revision no longer contains (for example oc-030's 'prompt states no endpoints' and oc-012's 'kiosks are dropped'). Those batch-5 texts are preserved unchanged; this re-check evaluates the emitted shipped text and supersedes the STATUS only.

evidence_classes.engine_executed: Buildable candidates: schema -> intent lint -> expander -> spec lint -> IPAM -> compile, run by verify_candidates.py.
evidence_classes.expected_refusal_source_traced: Refusal candidates: verify_candidates.py only asserts expected_intent is null. The named refusal code is traced in source, not executed end-to-end against Packet Tracer.
evidence_classes.live_packet_tracer: NOT RUN for any candidate in this re-check.

prior_issues: Static-routing requirement rested on a vague phrase; the intent could be graded on static while the prompt allowed a dynamic protocol.
Site host counts (8 head-office PCs, 5 branch PCs) were absent from the prompt.
shipped_text_check: Prompt now names static routing explicitly and forbids a dynamic protocol.
Prompt now states 8 head-office PCs and 5 branch PCs.
Expected behaviour over-claimed 'NAT at each'; corrected to one WAN block + NAT at the head office with the branch routed through it (CG-3).
entries.basis: Every prompt fact maps to the intent; the one engine limitation (single internet block) is now stated instead of over-claimed.

prior_issues: DHCP everywhere and OSPF specifically were not clearly stated by the prompt.
Per-floor host counts (6/10/4) were absent.
shipped_text_check: Prompt now says 'run OSPF rather than hand-written routes'.
Prompt now says everyone gets addresses automatically.
Prompt now states the 6 kiosks, 10 staff and 4 management desks.
entries.basis: The three flagged facts are explicit; staff/management separation is delivered as distinct pinned VLANs.

prior_issues: Intent requires DHCP at both sites but the prompt was silent on addressing.
PC counts (8 Karachi, 6 Lahore) were absent.
shipped_text_check: Prompt now says both sides receive IP automatically.
Prompt now states 8 Karachi computers and 6 Lahore computers.
entries.basis: Addressing and counts are explicit; static routing and internet-via-head-office are unambiguous.

prior_issues: Deliberate capability-boundary refusal with a null intent; a human must confirm the gap is real and that refusing a very common request is the intended eval signal.
The refusal needed to be explicit that it is a capability gap, not an ambiguity case.
The refusal needed a capability-version guard because it silently becomes wrong if guest isolation is implemented.
shipped_text_check: Candidate now records refusal_kind 'capability-gap' and a refused_intent_shape.
Expected behaviour names the exact refusal code and the engine site (expander.py:299).
Expected behaviour pins the verdict to the recorded engine commit and says to re-derive it if support lands.
Source trace confirms the code exists and fires when firewall.enabled and firewall.guest_isolation are set. This is not a live Packet Tracer execution.
entries.residual_owner_question: Do you want Gold to contain a named refusal for guest-WiFi isolation — a mainstream, reasonable request — knowing the refusal is source-traced but not live-PT-executed?
entries.basis: The capability gap is real in source; only the owner can decide that refusing this request is a desired evaluation signal.

prior_issues: Guest-facing kiosks named in the prompt were missing from the intent.
The intranet audience ('sales and warehouse can open it') was not expressed.
Four docked laptops were modelled as generic PCs.
The critical finance-isolation requirement coexists with connected routing and no ACL, so it is not enforced.
Section-labelled structure read like a form.
shipped_text_check: Intent now models 3 reception kiosks on the reception VLAN.
Expected behaviour states the audience clause is served by connected routing.
Docked laptops were removed; sales is now 22 wired desks, matching the intent.
Prompt was rewritten as a flowing client brief without schema-style headings.
Finance isolation is still not machine-verified; expected behaviour discloses UNKNOWN (CG-1).
entries.residual_owner_question: Accept a buildable brief whose critical 'finance is unreachable from anyone else' clause is recorded UNKNOWN (no inter-VLAN ACL capability), or rewrite/drop that guarantee?
entries.basis: All objective text defects are fixed. The remaining issue is a policy choice about shipping a critical isolation requirement the engine cannot verify.

prior_issues: Document skeleton and exclusion clauses duplicated oc-012 almost clause-for-clause (machine-generation tell).
shipped_text_check: Prompt is now a single natural narrative, not a labelled document scaffold.
Exclusions remain in the prompt but no longer share oc-012's section structure.
Accounts isolation is disclosed as UNKNOWN (CG-1) in expected behaviour.
entries.residual_owner_question: Accept a buildable two-site brief whose critical 'accounts not reachable by sales' clause is recorded UNKNOWN (CG-1)?
entries.basis: The style duplication is fixed. The remaining issue is the same isolation-policy choice as oc-012.

prior_issues: Wireless handhelds and forklift terminals are modelled as six tablets, a device-class substitution.
The warehouse system the ops devices talk to is not modelled.
The contractor VLAN has no hosts and 'internet only' is resolved by interpretation.
Inter-VLAN blocking is not enforced.
shipped_text_check: Expected behaviour records the tablet substitution as a forced mapping because HostDevice has no scanner/forklift value.
Expected behaviour explicitly says the WMS is out of scope for this candidate.
Expected behaviour records the empty contractor segment and the CG-3 single internet line.
Expected behaviour discloses inter-VLAN blocking as UNKNOWN (CG-1).
The candidate remains buildable and engine-verified.
entries.residual_owner_question: Accept the disclosed compromises (tablets for handhelds/forklifts, WMS out of scope, empty contractor segment, 'internet only' read as scope rather than an enforced block)?
entries.basis: The compromises are unavoidable in Schema v1 and are now disclosed; whether they are acceptable Gold content is an owner decision.

entries.prior_source: batch-3, re-read in batch-5 (batch-5 reason describes the pre-fix text)
prior_issues: Host groups (8/4/4 PCs) were invented because the prompt stated no endpoints.
DHCP was never stated.
shipped_text_check: Prompt now states 8 head-office computers and 4 at each branch.
Prompt now says every site gets IP automatically (DHCP).
NAT is a conventional planner default and is not asserted as a prompt fact.
entries.basis: Every previously invented host fact is now stated. The deliberate topology pair with oc-035 is handled as oc-035's residual, not this candidate's.

prior_issues: Duplicates oc-030's intent shape exactly (three sites, static routing, internet at HQ).
Host counts and DHCP were unstated.
shipped_text_check: Prompt now states 10 HQ PCs and 5 PCs per branch.
Prompt now says all get addresses automatically.
The intent remains structurally the same as oc-030 with different counts and site ids; this is documented as deliberate language pairing.
entries.residual_owner_question: Keep oc-030 and oc-035 as two Gold slots for one topology (English + Roman-Urdu variants), or keep only one?
entries.basis: The pair is intentional and documented, but counting one topology twice in a 100-slot gold set is an owner call.

entries.prior_source: batch-3, re-read in batch-5 (batch-5 reason describes the pre-fix duplicate)
prior_issues: Restated oc-011: same office-IoT-lighting scenario, same infrastructure, same expected behaviour.
IoT separation verifies UNKNOWN.
shipped_text_check: Prompt is now a retail shop with four till PCs and six LED units, not an office with staff PCs.
Intents differ in population and counts (oc-011: office staff + 4 lights; oc-040: tills + 6 lights).
Duplicate checks report no exact, normalized, intent-level or MinHash near-duplicate.
IoT placement is still UNKNOWN and is disclosed (CG-2).
entries.residual_owner_question: Keep both smart-LED IoT candidates (oc-011 office and oc-040 retail) even though the engine can only express smart_led and the network shape is similar?
entries.basis: The scenario is now distinct, but the underlying shape remains an IoT VLAN plus one host VLAN; whether that earns two Gold slots is an owner decision.

prior_issues: Expected behaviour offered an open menu (clarification preferred, stated assumption acceptable).
The clarification stopped at routing mode and did not request host counts or addressing.
shipped_text_check: Expected behaviour now gives one definite response: recommend a concrete mode, do not bounce the decision back.
It asks only for the missing build data: device counts, DHCP vs static, and where the internet line enters.
It forbids inventing site sizes and forbids presenting a silent pick as the user's choice.
entries.basis: The target response is now single and definite. Engine verification covers the null-intent rule only; this is a semantic judgement, not an executed refusal.

prior_issues: The second required issue ('must confirm the topology') asked for a fact the prompt already supplied (single office).
shipped_text_check: Expected behaviour now names exactly one issue: DSL + cable bonding is not expressible.
It explicitly says no topology question is required and that the ASA 5505 is acceptable for a single inside network.
It requires the model to ask which single access type to use.
entries.basis: The open ask was removed; the remaining response is definite and grounded in the single-valued access enum.

prior_issues: Limb (c) leaned on an unqualified generalisation about enforcement points.
No definite fallback deliverable was named.
shipped_text_check: All three limbs are now explicitly engine-scoped.
Expected behaviour names one fallback: build a plain guest subnet that makes no isolation promise.
It requires asking which requirement to drop: guest access to the internal site, or the internet-only guarantee.
It forbids deploying an appliance the user excluded and forbids silently dropping isolation.
entries.basis: The response is definite and engine-grounded. The refusal code is source-traced, not executed end-to-end.

prior_issues: Auditor addressing was invented as static while the prompt was silent.
The auditors-cannot-reach-accounting-or-servers requirement is not enforced by connected routing with no ACL.
The 'WAN for the accounting side only' scope was not expressed.
Section-labelled structure read like a form.
shipped_text_check: Auditor VLAN is now DHCP; the prompt names only the two servers as static.
Expected behaviour explains the DHCP choice and records the isolation clause as UNKNOWN (CG-1).
The accounting-only WAN scope is recorded as an inference/UNKNOWN rather than silently claimed.
Prompt was rewritten as a narrative brief.
Reception PCs sharing the accounting VLAN is recorded as an inference.
entries.residual_owner_question: Accept a buildable brief whose critical auditor-isolation clause and accounting-only WAN scope are recorded UNKNOWN, or rewrite/drop those guarantees?
entries.basis: The invented static addressing and the form-like structure are fixed. The isolation and egress-scope promises remain unverifiable by design.

prior_issues: Refusal expectation was internally inconsistent: guest isolation refused while the identically-shaped POS isolation was declared buildable.
Reason (c) (one internet block) read like a planner default rather than a hard refusal.
A human had to confirm whether refusal or build-plus-UNKNOWN is the single correct answer.
The refused shape invented a 'camerapanel' PC that the prompt never mentions.
shipped_text_check: Expected behaviour now explains the guest-vs-POS asymmetry: the guest clause requests the explicit guest_isolation capability, the POS clause does not.
It states that neither POS nor guest separation is machine-verified (CG-1), and that the POS separation must not be over-claimed.
CG-3 is now described as a reported limitation, not a silent build.
The invented camerapanel PC was removed from the refused shape; only the 3 cameras (as smart_led) remain.
entries.residual_owner_question: Is a named refusal the single correct answer for the guest-isolation clause, rather than building a plain guest subnet and reporting the isolation UNKNOWN? Confirm the POS separation is not over-claimed.
entries.basis: The internal contradiction and invented device are fixed. Refuse-vs-build-plus-UNKNOWN is a policy choice only the owner can make.

prior_issues: The intent invented 8 general PCs while the prompt never quantified the existing network.
Accounts VLAN addressing was unstated while the intent set DHCP.
File-server services went beyond the generic 'file server'.
Expected behaviour left an open 'may ask' about accounts-to-server access.
shipped_text_check: Prompt now states 8 general computers and 4 accounts computers.
Prompt now states accounts also take DHCP and the file server is static.
Expected behaviour now gives a definite build: FTP service on a static server VLAN, reached from both VLANs by connected routing; no clarification is required.
entries.basis: Counts and addressing are explicit and the open menu was removed.
